           …

faqs.a:
(a)
At the conclusion of a hearing under this article, the hearing officer may immediately
               render a verbal decision on the record, or may take the case under advisement and
               render a written decision no longer than 30 days after the conclusion of the hearing.
               To the extent practicable, the hearing officer's decision should include findings
               of fact relied on in reaching the decision. Unless otherwise required, however, the
               absence or incompleteness of findings of fact shall not constitute error. The decision
               shall be signed and dated by the hearing officer. A copy shall be mailed, first class
               postage pre-paid, to the last known address of each party, with a copy to each party's
               respective representative, if any. Facsimile or electronic transmission, with an original
               executed decision to follow, may be sent to the parties and shall serve fully as notice
               of the decision.
(b)
The hearing officer may request proposed findings and orders from the parties and
               may adopt and incorporate such findings and orders, or any portions thereof, as the
               findings and orders of the hearing officer as may be consistent with the evidence
               presented at the hearing.
(c)
In regard to those matters arising under
section 70-170
, the hearing officer shall confine the decision to determining whether cause exists,
               and whether the appointing authority acted arbitrarily and capriciously in determining
               the discipline imposed. The hearing officer shall have no authority to modify the
               discipline, but may make a recommendation consistent with the evidence presented at
               the hearing in accordance with the hearing officer's findings of fact. Subject to
               appeal as provided in
section 2-185
, the hearing officer may remand the matter to the appointing authority with a recommendation
               to take action in accordance with the hearing officer's conclusions and findings of
               fact. Such recommendation shall not constitute an order of the hearing officer under
section 2-173
(b).
(Code 1981, § 2-148; Ord. No. 3742, § 1, 5-6-2002; Ord. No. 3608, §§ 1, 2, 4-3-2003;
Ord. No. 4049, § 1, 1-8-2007
)
